prompt: Design a production-grade KVM/QEMU/libvirt virtualization operating system for a multi-tenant private-cloud compute pool. Cover workload contracts; hardware, firmware, kernel and KVM capability; QEMU and libvirt boundaries; host/domain capability inventory; domain identity and lifecycle; CPU, topology, NUMA, memory and overcommit; images, qcow2 chains, templates, cloud-init, storage and backup; bridges, taps, addressing and policy; management identity, transport, isolation and audit; placement, capacity, failure domains and noisy neighbors; migration, upgrades, fencing, HA and recovery; observability, incident diagnosis, evidence, cleanup, cost, governance and explicit refusal conditions.
directAnswer: Build the platform as a hierarchy of verified contracts. Start from user workload, correctness, availability, latency, recovery, isolation and lifecycle needs. Admit only hosts whose immutable hardware/firmware/kernel/KVM/emulator/libvirt/capability identity passes. Validate a versioned domain definition against both schema and domain capabilities, with unique UUID/MAC/NVRAM/storage ownership. Pin or govern CPU and machine compatibility, topology, NUMA, memory backing and resource controls. Manage images as immutable lineage: declared format, verified qcow2 chain, sanitized template, fresh per-instance datasource identity and independent restore-tested backup. Define the complete packet path and tenant policy. Use encrypted authenticated management, least privilege, process/storage/device isolation and protected audit. Place replicas across real failure domains, reserve capacity for declared failures and recovery, bound oversubscription, and watch per-host/per-domain/user saturation and stealing. Preflight migration for source/destination compatibility, storage, bandwidth, dirty rate, downtime, security and abort; prove one authority and service readiness afterward. Upgrade canaries with rollback. HA requires detection, fencing, restart or migration, storage/network readiness and measured user recovery. Refuse ambiguous identity, unsupported capability, unsafe shared writes, missing capacity, correlated failure domains, insecure control, untested restore/fencing or absent user evidence.
foundation: Virtualization is a layered resource and authority system. CPU flags do not prove KVM usability; KVM does not define a complete machine; QEMU Running does not prove the guest or application is ready; libvirt desired XML does not prove effective runtime; multiple hosts do not prove independent HA. Each transition needs evidence and an owner.
reasoningSteps: Define workload operations, state, data sensitivity, latency, throughput, availability, RPO/RTO and lifecycle.
Classify whether a VM is justified versus container, bare metal or managed service.
Inventory immutable host identity, architecture, CPU/NUMA, memory, devices, firmware settings and failure domains.
Verify kernel version/config/modules, KVM API and permissions rather than relying on flags.
Bind QEMU binary/version, accelerator, machine type, firmware and device-model compatibility.
Bind libvirt connection URI, driver, daemon, API/support contract and effective authorization.
Collect host capabilities and domain capabilities for every admitted host.
Version and schema-validate domain XML; compare desired, persistent and live state.
Guarantee unique name, UUID, MAC, IP, NVRAM and storage ownership.
Select CPU model and migration baseline from the intended host pool.
Validate sockets, cores, threads, vCPU count and licensing implications.
Place vCPU and memory with NUMA locality only from measured workload evidence.
Reserve non-guest host memory and account for QEMU, cache, huge pages and recovery.
Define CPU and memory overcommit/admission plus reclaim and contention behavior.
Track raw versus qcow2 trade-offs, virtual versus allocated size and thin-provision risk.
Declare image format and verify full backing lineage without unsafe autodetection.
Seal immutable templates after sanitizing identity, keys, logs, leases and cloud-init cache.
Generate unique per-instance metadata and verify every cloud-init boot stage.
Separate snapshot, clone, replication and independently restorable backup.
Map domain interface through tap, bridge or virtual switch, forwarding, physical NIC and return path.
Control MAC/IP/DHCP/DNS identity and tenant filtering.
Use least-privilege identities and encrypted authenticated local/remote libvirt paths.
Confine QEMU process, disks, devices, sockets and secrets with OS security controls.
Protect audit evidence from the same authority performing changes.
Map rack, power, host, switch, storage and management-plane correlation.
Use anti-affinity and reserve capacity for declared host/failure-domain loss.
Measure steal, run queue, memory pressure, I/O latency, thin-pool use and packet drops per domain and host.
Preflight migration for CPU/machine/firmware/device/storage/network/libvirt/QEMU compatibility.
Compare workload dirty rate with migration bandwidth and maximum downtime.
Secure migration transport and define cancellation, timeout, source/destination authority and cleanup.
Validate identity, storage, network, guest initialization, application and user flow after migration.
Use canary hosts for hypervisor, QEMU, libvirt, firmware and kernel upgrades.
Define rollback compatibility before changing machine types or storage formats.
For HA, detect failure independently and fence failed writers before restart.
Restore from independently tested backups when shared state or image lineage is damaged.
Measure detection, fence, boot, initialization and user recovery separately.
Correlate domain events, QEMU/libvirt logs, host pressure, storage/network evidence and application telemetry.
Preserve exact versions, XML, capabilities, image manifests, operations and timelines during incidents.
Govern quotas, ownership, deprecation, image lifecycle, patching, capacity and cost per tenant.
Prove exact cleanup of definitions, processes, sockets, networks, volumes, overlays, NVRAM and metadata.
Refuse when evidence cannot support identity, compatibility, isolation, capacity, recovery or user safety.
Keep every claim bounded to the tested host pool, topology, versions, workload and observation window.
seniorAnswer: I operate KVM as one kernel execution layer inside a governed compute platform. Admission binds host and domain capabilities, QEMU/libvirt/machine/CPU identity, unique VM and storage/network identity, safe image lineage and sanitized instance initialization. Placement uses real rack/power/network/storage domains and N+failure reserve, not host count. Management is encrypted, least privilege, confined and audited. Migration is a compatibility, storage, bandwidth, dirty-rate, authority and user-readiness workflow with abort. HA adds independent detection, fencing and measured recovery; backup adds independently tested historical restore. Per-domain and user evidence controls noisy neighbors and upgrades. I refuse ambiguous identity, unsupported features, shared writable state, insufficient reserve, insecure control or unproved recovery.
weakAnswer: Install KVM and libvirt on several large servers, use qcow2 for snapshots, enable CPU passthrough for speed, put all VMs on shared storage and let the cluster restart them after host failure.
whyWeak: It omits workload contracts, layered capability proof, image/template identity, network path, security, capacity, physical failure domains, migration compatibility, fencing, restore, user readiness, upgrades, audit and proof boundaries. Shared storage and automatic restart can amplify one failure.

evidence.signal: Immutable host manifest plus KVM/libvirt capabilities
evidence.proves: Covered host and driver features for that captured stack

evidence.signal: Validated domain definition and effective runtime inventory
evidence.proves: Desired and observed domain properties within collected coverage

evidence.signal: Image manifest, format, backing-chain and sanitization checks
evidence.proves: Covered image lineage and removed identity classes

evidence.signal: Capacity and failure-domain simulation with measured workload
evidence.proves: Recorded demand fits declared survivors under assumptions

evidence.signal: Migration effect, authority and user-flow journal
evidence.proves: Covered migration and service behavior for exact versions and load

evidence.signal: Fence receipt plus rejected old-path write
evidence.proves: Covered failed member lost named authority
evidence.doesNotProve: All external side effects are reconciled

evidence.proves: Named recovery artifact restored the covered flow

followUps.prompt: Where does KVM stop and QEMU begin?
followUps.answer: KVM exposes kernel acceleration and VM/vCPU/device interfaces. QEMU builds the userspace machine, device and block model and uses an accelerator such as KVM. Exact boundaries vary by device and configuration.
A floating alias can change device behavior after QEMU upgrades and break migration or guest assumptions. Pinning creates an explicit compatibility contract and planned upgrade path.
Only as a workload- and SLO-specific admission policy with measured concurrency, reclaim behavior, failure reserve and noisy-neighbor guardrails. Ratios alone are not safety evidence.
Independent detection, authoritative fencing, eligible destination and capacity, accessible correct state/network/identity, successful boot and initialization, and measured user-flow recovery.
Cloning machine identity, SSH keys, leases, logs or cloud-init cache creates duplicate identity, skipped first-boot work and secret exposure. Sanitization is verified before sealing the image.

rubric.observableEvidence: Connects user contract to hardware, KVM, QEMU, libvirt, guest and application
Binds immutable versions, capabilities, definition, runtime and compatibility
Designs topology, locality, admission, overcommit, reserve and pressure evidence
Controls format, lineage, templates, identity, cloud-init, backup and restore
Traces tap/bridge/forwarding and governs MAC/IP/DNS/tenant policy
Uses encrypted least privilege, confinement, secret and audit boundaries
Models real failure domains, N+failure reserve and noisy neighbors
Preflights compatibility/storage/rate/security and validates authority/user recovery
Includes detection, fencing, restart/restore, timeline, evidence and correctness
Defines quotas, ownership, lifecycle, cleanup, claim limits and no-run gates
